about: Per-model, per-layer sensitivity maps (the layer map). Each band names model layer ids (GGUF blk.N; models.<m>.layer_ids maps them to planner layers) and either a value with its provenance (tag MEASURED = ours, CLAIMED = someone else's published figure with a url, INFERRED-BY-US = derived by us) or fit: true (the planner fits the band from our measured quality points, src/model.js layerMap). A layer in no band is UNKNOWN, never zero. The value unit is the model's own 'unit' (for GLM: Maya's KL to the full model when that band alone keeps 5 routed experts). build.py copies this file to data.layer_maps.

trim_min_keep.src: CLAIMED Maya SETTINGS.md TRUNK_KEEP_MAP (abc09c7): keep 4 on layers 30-44 is the deepest trim they measured; deeper is extrapolation, so the trim proposer stops at 4

plan_margin.src: INFERRED: a layout the planner proposes from the map keeps its predicted KL below the bar by the largest KL residual of the map's own calibration points, and its predicted top-1 above the bar by the largest top-1 residual (the map is an inference; the margin is its measured miss)

glm.unit: KL to the full model when the band alone keeps 5 of 8 routed experts for experts not in VRAM (Maya-M, Maya's KL scale)

ref_miss_share.src: INFERRED: Maya's per-band KL was measured with Maya-M (116 GB) on a 3090 + 3060 (36 GB VRAM), so about half of the routed picks miss VRAM; their miss share is not published. Our snoopy k2e layout serves 51 % of reads from the GPU banks (planner tiers)

transfer.src: MEASURED lab notes (2026-10-20, snoopy k2e s1w, decode KL vs EXL3-3.05 exact, 928 positions): least squares through 0 of the served trim KL (served minus lane-only 0.00446) on the map's trim KL at transfer 1, three runs: A keep 7 on 26 + keep 4 on 27-44 measured 0.01481 vs 0.0124 (x1.19), B keep 5 on 27-44 0.00585 vs 0.0088 (x0.66), C keep 4 on 29-44 0.01096 vs 0.00657 (x1.67). The trim KL is convex in the dropped rank (keep 4 costs well over the linear 4/3 of keep 5), which the per-rank linear map does not model: a single factor leaves about 0.004 KL residual, so keep-4 points still read optimistic

top1_per_kl.src: MEASURED lab notes: top-1 lost per unit of served trim KL, least squares through 0 over runs A (0.9914 -> 0.96875 at trim KL 0.01481: 1.53), B (0.9838 at 0.00585: 1.30) and C (0.9752 at 0.01096: 1.48). The 2-bit line costs about 0.81 top-1 per KL: a trim drops whole expert picks, which flips the argmax faster than low-bit error does. mapQuality uses this rate for the trim part

trim.rank_drop: keep n drops ranks n..k-1 of the picks that miss VRAM: (k - n) / k of those picks (INFERRED: miss independent of rank)

glmlite.src: glm53-lane expert-trim e1160e7 (GLM53_NV_TRIM_KEEP, /nv_trim runtime switch; decode picks that miss VRAM, no renorm; 17 CPU tests OK in the serving image 2026-10-20), measured in lab notes runs A and B

bands.src: INFERRED: fitted from our two V4.1 KL points (lassie: the 1017 split, cold experts q2_K on every layer; the q3_K L0-13 / q2_K L14-39 requant). Two points, two bands: exactly determined, no residual to check it; q3_K on layers 0-13 is taken as lossless, as the 2-bit share line does
INFERRED: fitted from the same two V4.1 KL points (see layers 0-13)
